what: a side file a tool writes itself (scenes/multicam/silence --edl, caption's SRT and ASS, metadata's --chapters-out/--description-out, render's project and pack, verify/report's --report) was written with a plain open()/Path.write_text() after its output check, so a file another process created or edited at that path during the run was overwritten without --overwrite, and an interrupted write left a truncated sidecar
escaped: the replace-time recheck (#470) covered ffmpeg's own outputs and only two files a tool replaces itself (silence.py --timemap, export.py's fill/key); the side-file guards recorded the check but the plain write never compared it again, and no test wrote a sidecar after its check
mechanism: runner.write_sidecar stages a caller-named side file as a hidden sibling temp and puts it in place through replace_checked(), under the path's output lock after refuse_changed_output(); a target the check recorded absent is installed with os.link() so a file created in the gap is refused instead of replaced, an existing target keeps its permission bits, and the identity recorded (also in batch.py's report) is the staged file's, captured before the install; scenes, multicam, metadata, silence, caption, asr, _ass_overlay, render, report and verify call it instead of a plain open(); test_a_side_file_written_after_its_check_is_refused_and_one_left_alone_is_written, test_a_side_file_created_between_the_comparison_and_the_install_is_refused, test_the_identity_recorded_for_a_side_file_is_the_staged_file_not_a_foreign_one, test_a_side_file_keeps_the_mode_of_the_file_it_replaces and test_every_side_file_a_tool_writes_itself_goes_through_the_rechecked_helper pin the refusal, the install window, the record, the mode and the source sweep
